prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one single public service that tells every LLM “do you recommend this business?” — but you can both (A) put your business where AI systems pull data from, and (B) monitor/cross-check results. If you want one paid product that gets closest to both fixing and checking your presence across search engines and assistants, Yext is the most purpose-built option. For a low-cost approach combine Google Business Profile + Bing Places + Yelp + Google Alerts / Brand-monitoring tools and manual queries in major chat assistants.

Why Yext (best single paid option)
- Centralized “knowledge graph” that syndicates your business information across many directories, maps, and partners.
- Helps ensure consistent NAP, opening hours, services, menus, etc., which modern search engines and some assistants use.
- Integrates with Google, Microsoft/Bing, Apple, and other platforms that feed AI-powered search/assistant results.
- Has reporting so you can see which publishers/listings are live.

Free / low-cost practical approach (recommended if you don’t want Yext)
1. Claim and optimize profiles:
   - Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Facebook, TripAdvisor (if relevant).
2. Add structured data on your website:
   - LocalBusiness JSON‑LD schema, service/product markup, FAQ schema.
3. Encourage reviews on Google/Yelp/etc. (high-quality reviews improve likelihood of appearing in recommendations).
4. Earn citations and quality backlinks:
   - Trusted directories, local news, industry sites, a Wikipedia page if notable.
5. Monitor mentions:
   - Google Alerts (free), and paid monitors like Brand24, Mention, Talkwalker for broader coverage.
6. Test the assistants directly:
   - Ask Google Bard, Bing Chat (and Alexa/Siri where relevant) queries such as “Recommend a [service] in [city]” or “Best [type of business] near me” and see if your business is returned or cited. For ChatGPT specifically, try queries in ChatGPT (noting standard ChatGPT may not browse the web and may rely on training data).

How to check specifically whether ChatGPT recommends you
- If you mean the non-browsing ChatGPT: it uses training data and won’t reflect recent listings. There’s no API to query “does your model recommend X?” except by asking it directly, but answers reflect learned patterns, not live verification.
- If you mean ChatGPT/Bing/Google with browsing or live web retrieval: ask them live and look for citations/links (Bing and Bard will often cite sources).

Which monitoring tools to consider
- Yext (paid, best for authoritative syndicated presence)
- BrightLocal / Moz Local (local SEO + monitoring)
- Brand24, Mention, Awario, Talkwalker (brand mention monitoring)
- Google Alerts (free)

Recommended quick plan (for most small businesses)
1. Claim Google Business Profile and Bing Places (if you only do one free thing, do GBP).
2. Add schema on your website and a clear “Services / Locations” page.
3. Get 10–20 good Google/Yelp reviews.
4. Set up Google Alerts and one paid monitor (Brand24 or Mention).
5. Run manual checks in Bing Chat and Google Bard for typical user queries and use Yext if you want a single-management paid solution.

If you tell me your business type and city, I can give example search prompts to test each assistant and an ordered checklist tuned for your industry.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
